title: CGT roll-overs — navigator for the remaining roll-overs
summary: Decision-tree navigator covering all Subdivision 124 roll-overs (except 124-B compulsory acquisition and 124-M scrip for scrip, which have separate maps), plus Subdivisions 122-B (partners to company), 125-B (demerger), 126-B/C/D/G (same-asset roll-overs) and 128-A/B (deceased estates). Guides from transaction type to the applicable roll-over with key conditions and consequences per branch.

nodes.label: CGT event has happened — you want to defer (roll-over) the capital gain
nodes.body: A roll-over defers a capital gain (or loss) until a later CGT event. Replacement-asset roll-overs (Div 112 Subdiv C) involve the original asset being replaced; same-asset roll-overs (Div 112 Subdiv D) involve the same asset being transferred. This navigator covers roll-overs under Subdivs 122-B, 124-C/D/E/F/I/J/K/L/N/P/Q/R/S, 125-B, 126-B/C/D/G and 128-A/B.

nodes.label: What type of transaction gives rise to the CGT event?
nodes.body: Navigate to the correct roll-over category: (1) Replacement asset — you receive a new asset in place of the original; (2) Shares, units and entity interests — exchanges, conversions or demergers of shares/units; (3) Entity restructures — transfers between group companies, trusts or super funds; (4) Special assets — compulsory acquisition (separate map), scrip for scrip (separate map); (5) Deceased estates — asset devolves to legal personal representative or passes to a beneficiary.

nodes.label: Replacement asset: what kind of original asset is being replaced?
nodes.body: Replacement asset roll-overs (s 112-115 table): individual/trustee to wholly-owned company (item 1, ss 122-40 to 122-65); partners to wholly-owned company (item 2, ss 122-150 to 122-195); compulsory acquisition (item 4, Subdiv 124-B); statutory licences (item 5); strata title (item 6); same-company share/unit exchange (item 7); rights/options exchange (item 8); change of incorporation (item 11); Crown leases (item 12); depreciating assets (item 13); prospecting/mining (item 14); scrip-for-scrip (item 14A); trust restructure (item 14B); MDO (item 14BB); stapled interests (item 14BC); water entitlements (item 14BD); demergers (item 14C, Div 125); Div 615 interposed company / units-for-shares (items 14D/14E); securities lending (item 15, s 26BC). Eligibility conditions for each roll-over are in the cited provisions — check before applying.

nodes.label: Shares, units or entity interests: what is the nature of the exchange?
nodes.body: Roll-overs for shares, units and entity interests include: exchange of shares in the same company (124-E), exchange of rights/options (124-F), change of incorporation (124-I), trust to company (124-N), MDO membership exchange (124-P), stapled interest exchange (124-Q), demerger (125-B), and partners disposing of assets to a company (122-B).

nodes.label: Entity restructure: what kind of entity is involved?
nodes.body: Same-asset roll-overs (Div 126) apply to transfers between entities in the same group or restructures: wholly-owned group company transfers (126-B), trust deed changes (126-C), small superannuation fund transfers (126-D), and trust-to-trust asset transfers (126-G). These are same-asset roll-overs where the asset continues in new hands.

nodes.label: Special assets: compulsory acquisition or scrip for scrip?
nodes.body: Two major roll-overs have their own dedicated maps: Subdivision 124-B (compulsory acquisition, loss or destruction — see separate map) and Subdivision 124-M (scrip for scrip exchange of shares in a takeover — see separate map). Other special-asset roll-overs are covered in the replacement asset branch.

nodes.label: Deceased estate: has a CGT asset devolved to a legal personal representative or beneficiary?
nodes.body: Deceased estate: has a CGT asset devolved to a legal personal representative (LPR) or passed to a beneficiary? If no CGT asset devolved or passed, the deceased-estate roll-over analysis does not apply — normal CGT rules govern the estate.

nodes.label: 124-C: New statutory licences (s 124-140)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available when your ownership of one or more statutory licences ends (CGT event C2) and you are issued one or more new licences authorising substantially similar activity (s 124-140(1)). The new licence must be taxable Australian property if the original was. Consequence: the gain is disregarded; the new licence inherits the original's cost base per Subdiv 124-A.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-D: Strata title conversion (s 124-190)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available if you own property giving a right to occupy a unit in a building, the building is subdivided into stratum units, and the owner transfers the corresponding stratum unit to you (s 124-190(1)). Consequence: the gain is disregarded; the first element of the new stratum unit's cost base includes what you paid plus the original property's cost base under Subdiv 124-A.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-J: Crown leases (s 124-570)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available when the holder of a Crown lease over land has the lease renewed, extended or converted to an estate in fee simple (s 124-570 — What this Subdivision is about). Consequence: the gain is disregarded; the replacement lease or estate in fee simple inherits the original's cost base per Subdiv 124-A.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-K: Depreciating assets roll-over (s 124-655)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available for a depreciating asset attached to land held under a quasi-ownership right (granted by an exempt Australian or foreign government agency) when the right expires or is terminated and you are granted a new quasi-ownership right or an estate in fee simple (s 124-655). No roll-over if already covered by Subdiv 124-J or 124-L. Consequence per Subdiv 124-A.

nodes.label: 124-L: Prospecting and mining entitlements (s 124-700)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available when a prospecting or mining entitlement expires or is surrendered and it is replaced by a new one (s 124-700 — What this Subdivision is about). Operative provisions: ss 124-705 to 124-730. Consequence: gain disregarded; the cost base of the original entitlement carries into the new entitlement per Subdiv 124-A.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-R: Water entitlements (s 124-1100)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available if a CGT event happens because of something occurring in relation to water entitlements (s 124-1100 — What this Subdivision is about). Three cases: replacement water entitlements, reduction in water entitlements, and variation to a CGT asset. Consequence: gain or loss disregarded; cost base carries over.

nodes.label: FACET — Subdiv 124-S is NOT in the s 112-115 replacement-asset table
nodes.body: s 112-115 does not list Subdivision 124-S (interest realignment arrangements). Check the specific 124-S provisions directly if an interest realignment is proposed — it is not one of the table roll-overs.

nodes.label: 122-B: Partners disposing of assets to a wholly-owned company (ss 122-150 to 122-195)
nodes.body: s 112-115 item 2 (replacement asset): disposal or creation of assets by partners to a wholly-owned company — ss 122-150 to 122-195. Same-asset component: s 112-150 item 4 — transfer of a partnership CGT asset to a wholly-owned company, ss 122-200 and 122-205. Individual/trustee to wholly-owned company: s 112-115 item 1, ss 122-40 to 122-65.

nodes.label: 124-I: Change of incorporation (s 124-510)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available for members of a body that is incorporated under one law and is converted to, or replaced with, a body incorporated under another law (s 124-510 — What this Subdivision is about). Consequence: shares in the new corporation replace the original interests with a cost base transfer per Subdiv 124-A.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-N: Trust to company roll-over (s 124-850)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available when a trust disposes of all its assets to a company and units/interests in the trust are replaced by shares in the company (s 124-850 — What this Subdivision is about). Also available for 2+ trusts disposing to a single company. Note: effect may be reversed if trust does not cease within 6 months (CGT event J1, s 104-195).

nodes.label: 124-P: MDO membership exchange (s 124-975)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available if you exchange your interest as a member of a Medical Defence Organisation (MDO) for an interest in another MDO (s 124-975 — What this Subdivision is about). You can only choose the roll-over if you would have made a capital gain from the exchange. Consequence: gain disregarded; new interest inherits the original's cost base.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 124-Q: Exchange of stapled ownership interests (s 124-1040)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available if you own stapled ownership interests and, as a result of a reorganisation, you stop owning those interests and acquire ownership interests in an interposed unit trust (s 124-1040 — What this Subdivision is about). Consequence: gain disregarded; new interests inherit the stapled interests' cost base.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 125-B: Demerger roll-over (s 125-55)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available if you own an ownership interest in the head entity of a demerger group, a demerger happens, and you acquire a new or replacement interest in the demerged entity (s 125-55(1)). Not available if you are a foreign resident and the new interest is not taxable Australian property (s 125-55(2)). Consequence: gain is disregarded; cost base adjustments under s 125-80.

nodes.label: 126-B: Wholly-owned group roll-over (s 126-45)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available for the transfer of a CGT asset between two companies that are members of the same wholly-owned group, where at least one is a foreign resident (s 126-40 — What this Subdivision is about). CGT events must be A1, B1, D1, D2, D3 or F1 (s 126-45(2)). Consequence: gain disregarded; same-asset roll-over — the asset's cost base continues unchanged.

nodes.label: 126-C: Trust deed changes (s 126-125)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available for a CGT event that happens because of an amendment to or replacement of the trust deed of a complying approved deposit fund, complying superannuation fund, or a fund that accepts worker entitlement contributions (s 126-125 — What this Subdivision is about). Consequence: gain disregarded; same-asset roll-over.

nodes.label: 126-D: Small superannuation fund transfers (s 126-140)
nodes.body: A roll-over is available when an interest in a small superannuation fund is subject to a payment split under the Family Law Act and the non-member spouse serves a waiver notice, resulting in a CGT asset transfer to another complying superannuation fund (s 126-140(1)-(2)). Consequence: gain disregarded; same-asset roll-over.

nodes.label: 126-G: Transfer of assets between certain trusts (s 126-215)
nodes.body: A roll-over may be available when CGT assets are transferred between certain trusts (s 126-215 — What this Subdivision is about). Requirements: s 126-225 (when a roll-over may be chosen); the beneficiaries' entitlements must not be discretionary (s 126-230). Exceptions in s 126-235. Consequence: same-asset roll-over — cost base carries over between trusts.
definitions: cost base of a cgt asset

nodes.label: 128-A/B: Deceased estates — effect on LPR or beneficiary (s 128-15)
nodes.body: When a CGT asset owned just before death devolves to the legal personal representative (LPR) or passes to a beneficiary (ss 128-A, 128-B), the recipient is taken to have acquired the asset on the day of death (s 128-15(2)). Any gain or loss the LPR makes when the asset passes to a beneficiary is disregarded (s 128-15(3)). The cost base is generally the market value at death (s 128-15(4)).

nodes.label: 124-M: Scrip for scrip — see separate map
nodes.body: Subdivision 124-M provides replacement-asset roll-over for exchanges of shares or units in a takeover/takeover bid. See the separate map for Subdivision 124-M (scrip for scrip). Key condition: the exchanging entity must acquire 80%+ of the target; gain is deferred into the new shares/units.

nodes.label: 124-C roll-over applied — gain deferred into new statutory licence
nodes.body: The gain is disregarded; the new licence inherits the original licence's cost base (or pre-CGT status) per Subdiv 124-A general rules. The deferred gain will be brought to account when the new licence is later disposed of.

nodes.label: Roll-over applied — gain deferred
nodes.body: The relevant roll-over has been chosen and applied. The gain is disregarded; the new asset or transferred asset inherits the appropriate cost base. Refer to the specific Subdivision for any recapture events (e.g., CGT events J2, J5, J6) that may later bring the deferred gain to account.

nodes.body: s 112-115 item 14D: exchange of shares in one company for shares in an interposed company; item 14E: exchange of units in a unit trust for shares in a company — both under Division 615.

nodes.label: No deceased-estate roll-over — normal CGT rules
nodes.body: If no CGT asset devolved to an LPR or passed to a beneficiary, the deceased-estate roll-over path does not apply; the estate is taxed under normal CGT rules.
